newsitem.title: THAILAND: Hundreds of Karen refugees seriously ill in camps.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of Karen refugees seriously ill in camps.

text.p: The Thai public health ministry said on Sunday more than 1,700 Karen refugees fleeing fighting in Burma were ill with diarrhoea, flu and malaria at their rugged settlement areas inside Thailand.
Two had died recently from diarrhoea, the ministry said.

It said in a statement that a Thai medical team sent to care for more than 3,000 refugees living in camps in Thailand's Kanchanaburi and Ratchaburi provinces found that 1,791 ethnic Karens were seriously ill.
"Among the sick, 1,003 were afflicted with diarrhoea and two of them died recently," it said, adding that 575 suffered from flu and 134 were infected with malaria.

Nearly 100,000 Karen refugees had fled to Thailand from fighting between the Karen National Union (KNU) and Burmese government troops. Their sprlawing settlement camps are run by international relief agencies and the Karen Refugees Committee (KRC), a KNU affiliate.
The KRC last week called on the U.N. High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) to run the camps, hoping its role would discourage possible Burmese attacks on the settlements.
UNHCR, which has provided humanitarian assistance for the refugees, said its officials would travel to the Thai-Burmese border next week to inspect the camps.
